title: Benedicite (Canticle of the Three Children)
text:
Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord:
praise and exalt him above all forever.

Angels of the Lord, bless the Lord:
you heavens, bless the Lord.
All you waters above the heavens, bless the Lord:
all you hosts of the Lord, bless the Lord.

Sun and moon, bless the Lord:
stars of heaven, bless the Lord.
Every shower and dew, bless the Lord:
all you winds, bless the Lord.

Fire and heat, bless the Lord:
cold and chill, bless the Lord.
Dew and rain, bless the Lord:
frost and chill, bless the Lord.

Ice and snow, bless the Lord:
nights and days, bless the Lord.
Light and darkness, bless the Lord:
lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

Let the earth bless the Lord:
praise and exalt him above all forever.
Mountains and hills, bless the Lord:
every thing that springs from the earth, bless the Lord.

You springs, bless the Lord:
seas and rivers, bless the Lord.
You dolphins and all water creatures, bless the Lord:
all you birds of the air, bless the Lord.
All you beasts, wild and tame, bless the Lord:
you sons of men, bless the Lord.

O Israel, bless the Lord:
praise and exalt him above all forever.
Priests of the Lord, bless the Lord:
servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.
Spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord:
holy men of humble heart, bless the Lord.

Hananiah, Azariah, Mishael, bless the Lord:
praise and exalt him above all forever.
For he has delivered us from death:
and saved us from the power of death.
He has saved us from the fiery furnace:
and delivered us from the midst of the burning flame.

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good:
for his mercy endures forever.
Bless the Lord, God of gods:
praise and exalt him above all forever.
Blessed are you, Lord, the God of our fathers:
praiseworthy and glorious above all forever.
Blessed is your holy and glorious name:
praiseworthy and exalted above all forever.

translation.latin:
Benedicite, omnia opera Domini, Domino:
laudate et superexaltate eum in saecula.

Angeli Domini, benedicite Domino:
caeli, benedicite Domino.
Aquae omnes, quae super caelos sunt, benedicite Domino:
omnes virtutes Domini, benedicite Domino.

Sol et luna, benedicite Domino:
stellae caeli, benedicite Domino.
imber et ros, benedicite Domino:
omnes spiritus Dei, benedicite Domino.

Ignis et aestus, benedicite Domino:
frigus et aestus, benedicite Domino.
Rores et pruinæ, benedicite Domino:
pruina et nives, benedicite Domino.

Glacies et nives, benedicite Domino:
noctes et dies, benedicite Domino.
Lux et tenebrae, benedicite Domino:
fulgura et nubes, benedicite Domino.

Terra, benedic Domino:
laudate et superexaltate eum in saecula.
Montes et colles, benedicite Domino:
omnia quae germinant in terra, benedicite Domino.

Fontes, benedicite Domino:
mare et flumina, benedicite Domino.
Cete, et omnia quae moventur in aquis, benedicite Domino:
omnes volucres caeli, benedicite Domino.
Omnes bestiae et pecora, benedicite Domino:
filii hominum, benedicite Domino.

Israel, benedic Domino:
laudate et superexaltate eum in saecula.
Sacerdotes Domini, benedicite Domino:
servi Domini, benedicite Domino.
Spiritutes et animae iustorum, benedicite Domino:
sancti et humiles corde, benedicite Domino.

Anania, Azaria, Misael, benedicite Domino:
laudate et superexaltate eum in saecula.
Quia eripuit nos de inferno:
et salvavit nos de manu mortis.
Et eripuit nos de medio ignis ardentis:
et de medio flammae eruit nos.

Confitemini Domino, quoniam bonus:
quoniam in saeculum misericordia eius.
Benedicite Deum deorum:
laudate et superexaltate eum in saecula.
Benedictus es, Domine, Deus patrum nostrorum:
et laudabilis et superexaltatus in saecula.
Et benedictum nomen gloriae tuae sanctum:
et superexaltatum in saecula.

attribution: From the Book of Daniel 3:57-88 (Deuterocanonical), Song of the Three Young Men in the fiery furnace
notes: The Benedicite is the Canticle of the Three Children (Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego) who were thrown into the fiery furnace for refusing to worship King Nebuchadnezzar's golden image. It is a beautiful hymn calling all creation to bless the Lord. It is used in the Liturgy of the Hours and in Anglican morning prayer.
description: The Benedicite is a canticle from Daniel calling all creation to bless the Lord
